skill.name: nature-paper2ppt
skill.description: Turns scientific papers, abstracts, figure legends, or reading notes into concise simplified Chinese PPTX decks for journal clubs, lab meetings, and academic talks. It uses a Nature-style evidence narrative, chooses key figures, writes speaker notes, and performs a PPTX self-review pass.
skill.summary: Create Chinese research presentation decks from scientific papers.
skill.author: Community contribution, refactored into static/dynamic layers

security_audit.summary: Most static command, reconnaissance, archive, and entropy alerts are false positives from Markdown formatting, Chinese documentation, and PPTX validation guidance. The confirmed issue is a fixed parent-directory dependency on ../_shared/core/terminology-ledger.md, which can load content outside the reviewed skill package.

remediation.suggestion: Move terminology-ledger.md into the skill package or a declared reviewed dependency, then update manifest.yaml, SKILL.md, and README.md.
Ensure every automatically loaded reference is bundled with the published skill and covered by the marketplace review.

content.user_title: Create Chinese PPTX Decks From Research Papers
content.value_statement: Researchers often need a clear presentation from a dense paper. This skill turns papers into concise Chinese PPTX decks with figures, notes, and QA checks.
actual_capabilities: Classifies papers into discovery, methods, resource, clinical, materials, or review arcs.
Creates simplified Chinese slide titles, concise bullets, captions, takeaways, and speaker notes.
Selects key figures or tables that support the paper argument.
Builds an editable PPTX deck with source labels and a QA report.
Runs a self-review pass for figure readability, text overflow, slide bounds, and package validity.
limitations: Requires readable source material; scanned PDFs may need OCR or user-provided text.
Generated figure crops still need human review for scientific accuracy.
Does not replace copyright checks for reusing published figures.
Rendered slide preview depends on an available headless renderer.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Journal Club Talk
use_cases.description: Convert a new paper into a 10-14 slide Chinese deck with speaker notes and key figures.

use_cases.title: Build a Lab Meeting Briefing
use_cases.description: Summarize a paper for a group meeting with claims, evidence, limitations, and discussion prompts.

use_cases.title: Create a Seminar Paper Report
use_cases.description: Turn a dense review or methods paper into a structured teaching deck with a clear narrative arc.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Paper Deck
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with one paper PDF.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 10-14 slide simplified Chinese PPTX from this paper PDF. Include key figures, source labels, and speaker notes.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Journal Club Slides
prompt_templates.prompt: Make a Chinese journal club deck for a 15 minute talk. Classify the paper type first, then build the PPTX around the main evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt for a Methods Paper
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a specific paper type.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the methods paper arc. Explain the problem, method design, validation, benchmarks, limitations, and reuse value in a concise Chinese PPTX.

prompt_templates.title: Revise and Audit an Existing Draft
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with an existing deck or template.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my draft deck as the base. Improve figure readability, reduce text overflow, add speaker notes, and produce a short QA report.

output_examples.input: A Nature paper PDF and a request for a group meeting presentation.
output_examples.output: A 12-slide simplified Chinese PPTX with title slide, evidence slides, discussion slide, speaker notes, and QA report.

output_examples.input: An abstract, results text, and figure legends from a methods paper.
output_examples.output: A concise PPTX that explains the method problem, workflow, validation results, limitations, and reuse value.

output_examples.input: A review article and a request for a seminar deck.
output_examples.output: A schematic-led Chinese deck that maps themes, controversies, author synthesis, and future directions.

best_practices: Provide the full paper PDF, figure legends, or structured notes when possible.
Tell the skill the talk length, audience level, and preferred slide count.
Review generated figure crops and source labels before presenting the deck.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to invent missing results, numbers, mechanisms, or figure details.
Do not force every paper into the same slide template.
Do not use it as a copyright clearance tool for published figures.

faq.question: Does this skill create an actual PPTX file?
faq.answer: Yes. The intended output is an editable PPTX deck, not only an outline or script.

faq.question: What language does it use by default?
faq.answer: It writes simplified Chinese slides while preserving important technical terms in English when useful.

faq.question: Can it handle papers outside biology?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes arcs for methods, resource, clinical, materials, discovery, and review papers.

faq.question: Will it extract every figure from a PDF?
faq.answer: No. It selects only figures and tables that support the presentation argument.

faq.question: Can it use an existing PPTX template?
faq.answer: Yes. A user-provided template can guide the final deck when it fits the content.

faq.question: Does it verify slide quality?
faq.answer: It runs a self-review pass for text overflow, figure readability, slide bounds, and PPTX package validity.
